note: HIDDEN ground truth for Trial C (comprehension). Answerer arms see only the questions; the judge sees the answers.

questions.q: Can an account's balance ever become negative? What prevents it?
questions.a: No. Both withdraw and transfer reject the operation if the balance is less than the amount, checked before any money moves, so a balance never goes below zero.

questions.q: Is a transfer atomic (all-or-nothing)? What happens on a failed transfer?
questions.a: Yes. A transfer debits the source and credits the destination together; if it fails (for example insufficient funds), neither balance changes.

questions.q: If you try to withdraw more than the balance, what happens to the balance?
questions.a: Nothing. The withdrawal is rejected with an error and the balance is left unchanged.

questions.q: Is the total amount of money conserved by a transfer, and why?
questions.a: Yes. A transfer subtracts an amount from the source and adds the same amount to the destination, so the sum of all balances is unchanged.

questions.q: Can money be transferred from an account to itself?
questions.a: No. A same-account transfer is rejected.

questions.q: What makes an amount valid for a deposit, withdrawal or transfer?
questions.a: It must be a strictly positive integer in minor units. Zero, negative, and non-integer amounts are rejected.

questions.q: What happens if you deposit into an account that was never opened?
questions.a: It is rejected as an unknown account, and no balance changes.

questions.q: Can the same account id be opened twice?
questions.a: No. Opening an account that already exists is rejected.
